Class Complex

java.lang.Object
sysmlinjava.common.SysMLAnything
sysmlinjava.attributetypes.SysMLAttributeType
sysmlinjava.attributetypes.Complex
All Implemented Interfaces:
ObservableAttribute
public class Complex extends SysMLAttributeType
SysMLinJava's representation of the value type for complex values, i.e. two (real and imaginary) values of double type.

This representation of the complex number type is for a generic complex number as used in SysML. Hence the use of two Java doubles for its value. This SysML complex number is not the same as two java float, double, Float or Double types as SysML does not discriminate between bit-lengths of real or floating- point numeric types as does the Java language.

Note: as an observableValueType this value type can be "observed" by other objects. ValueObservers call the addValueObserver() operation to be notiified (called-back) by the Complex object of any change in its value. This notification will only occur if and when the Complex value is changed by a call to the setValue() operation. So, while the Complex value is publicly accessible and can be changed by direct assignment, the setValue() operation must be used if ValueObservers are to be notified of the change.

    • createUnits

      protected void createUnits()
      Description copied from class: SysMLAttributeType
      Required operation to create/assign the units attribute for this attribute type. The units variable should be assigned with the name of a SysMLUnit instance located in an extension of the SysMLUnits class. An example is as follows: 
      @Override
protected void createUnits()
{
        units = SysMLinJavaUnits.FeetCubic;
}
